text:
P0 CATALOG LATENCY — ANSWERED. /research/early-access DOES NOT USE THE BULK PATH. It still runs the per-product fan-out. Measured at origin 8fcebf5 by reading the wiring end to end, not inferred.

THE FOUNDER ASKED: prove the EA catalog uses the new ~3-query bulk/cached path and not the old ~3,306-query path. ANSWER: IT USES THE OLD ONE. The bulk fix was applied to a DIFFERENT door.

THE CHAIN, every link verified:
1. server/index.ts:640 wires BulkCatalogPricingSource to masterOfferingCatalogPricingSource — the master-offerings v2 catalog. That is where the 3,306 -> 3 work landed.
2. The Early Access door is EARLY_ACCESS_CATALOG_PATH = /api/research/early-access/catalog (register.ts:201), sourced from createEarlyAccessCatalogSourceForDeployment.
3. That resolves to createProductionEarlyAccessCatalogSource (product-control-source.ts:390-396), which constructs ProductControlCatalogSource with catalog: createProductionProductControlReader().
4. That reader is LiveProductControlReader.readCatalog() in server/research/catalog/product-control-reader.ts:146. It does NOT touch BulkCatalogPricingSource anywhere.

THE ARITHMETIC, from the code:
- readCatalog does repository.list() once for summaries (line 147)
- then `await Promise.all(exact.map(p => this.readStableDetail(p)))` (line 165) — ONE readStableDetail PER PUBLISHED PRODUCT
- readStableDetail (line 126) does repository.get(id) TWICE per product: a double read whose two snapshots are compared for stability
- then repository.list() AGAIN for verification (line 168)

So: 2 list calls + (2 x publishedProducts) get calls. PROJECT_STATE reports publishedProducts 217, activeVariants 417. That is 2 + 434 = 436 round trips minimum for one catalog page, before whatever repository.get() itself expands into for variants, prices and media — which is where the original 3,306 figure came from.

436+ sequential-ish network round trips to Supabase is a complete and sufficient explanation for a 30-60 second catalog on a phone. There is no cache and no stale-while-revalidate on this path; BulkCatalogPricingSource has all of that and this door never calls it.

WHY IT HID: the read-amplification regression test (server/research/pricing/catalog-read-amplification.test.ts) proves three queries for a 420-row page — but it exercises BulkCatalogPricingSource, not this reader. The test is true and the door is still slow, because they are different code paths. That is the same unit-green/door-broken class as the legal port and the pricing viewer.

I AM NOT FIXING IT: server/research/catalog/** is claude-fable-s7's ACTIVE lease (CATALOG-ACTION-UNIFICATION). This is theirs or the lead's to take. I am not crossing an active lease on the launch-critical path, and I have already duplicated two lanes today by moving before checking.

WHAT I WOULD DO, for whoever takes it — cheapest first:
1. The double read in readStableDetail is a 2x multiplier on the whole fan-out. If the stability check is not load-bearing for the EA display path, halving it is a one-line win.
2. The real fix is the same shape as BulkCatalogPricingSource: one bulk read of published products plus their variants and prices, a short-lived shared snapshot, stale-while-revalidate, and the empty-success guard so a successful empty read cannot poison a healthy snapshot.
3. Whatever lands needs a read-amplification test against THIS reader, not against the bulk source, or the same gap reopens.

I CANNOT MEASURE THE LIVE NUMBERS the founder asked for (TTFB, catalog API duration, first card, first price). That needs a running deployment with real credentials, which is production and not mine. Somebody on P0-G with a working environment should take the measurements; this report is the code-path proof that explains what they will see.

NOT a frontend problem. Do not chase this in React.
